- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) and forecast is rising, cap upward movement at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to prevent false optimism.  
- After a sharp spike in price (forecast > +5% from prior 30d mean), apply a 3–5 day mean-reversion bias downward by 1–3% per day.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and forecast is trending, align with 14-day moving average to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.  
- If forecast consistently exceeds true outcome by >3% over 3 consecutive days, reduce next-day forecast by 2–4% to correct for momentum bias.  
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8, 0.1, 0.7), apply a “sentiment dampening” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% for each low sentiment day following a high.
